summary:
# NOTES: THE SQUIRE'S DAUGHTER (Silas K. Hocking, 1906, Frederick Warne; illus. Arthur Twidle; Gutenberg #36384). Single book, 43 chapters. Trailing ads: *The Flaming Sword*, *Pioneers* (press quotes only).

## Characters
- **Ralph Penlogan**: 20 at start; son of David; Cornish, self-educated, chemist/mineralogist, proud, resentful of class injustice. Later rich mine manager.
- **David Penlogan**: father, gentle Methodist, Hillside Farm tenant on Polskiddy Downs; dies of stroke.
- **Mary Penlogan**: mother; dies in workhouse.
- **Ruth Penlogan**: sister; dark-brown eyes; sewing maid; later engaged to William Menire.
- **Dorothy Hamblyn**: squire's daughter, 17–18; imperious; rides mare **Jess** (gift from Probus). Thrown at Treliskey gate; later reformed, loves Ralph.
- **Sir John Hamblyn**: baronet, squire, Lord of the Manor; grasping, in debt (Turf, Stock Exchange, money-lenders); later "lord of manor" = Lord St. Goram confusion in text; exiled to Boulogne.
- **Geoffrey Hamblyn**: son, indolent.
- **Lord Probus**: 60, brewer, bald, iron-grey military moustache, Rostrevor Castle; betrothed to Dorothy.
- **Dr. Barrow**: doctor. **William** the coachman. **James**: boy in buttons. **Billy**: attendant of bath-chair/donkey.
- **Molly Udy**: source of gossip.
- **Julian Seccombe**: parson's son, "life" on lease; wounded in Egypt, dies.
- **Rev. John Seccombe**: vicar of St. Goram.
- **Lawyer Doubleday**: "life" lost (son drowned).
- **Billy Penlogan**: child "life" (scarlet fever).
- **William Jenkins**: farmer; takes Hillside at Michaelmas.
- **Budda**: policeman. **Bilkins**: Sir John's gardener. **Jim Brewer**: miner; confesses shooting Sir John.
- **William Menire**: general dealer, St. Goram shop, ~36; devoted to Ruth; mother dies.
- **Amos Bice**: auctioneer, landlord of Penlogan cottage.
- **Mr. Tregonning**: magistrate. **Mr. Thomas**: relieving officer.
- **Mr. Varcoe**: Quaker, Ruth's employer at St. Hilary.
- **Robert Telfer**: contractor, Perranpool; daughter **Mary Telfer** (cheerful, bright).
- **Sir John Liskeard**: barrister/MP, Ralph's counsel.
- **Sam Tremail**: William's cousin, Pentudy farmer, 26; proposes to Ruth, refused.
- **Uncle Ned**: Tremail's uncle (politics).
- **Archie Temple**: Dorothy's suitor (nephew of earl).
- **Dowager Duchess of Flint**: Dorothy's employer.
- **Peter Ladock**: neighbouring farmer. **Daniel Rickard**: freeholder sold to company.
- **Dick Lowry**: smith. **Mr. Hooker**: gave shooting permission. **Dr. Roscommon**: famous surgeon.
- **Jess**: Dorothy's mare.

## Places
St. Goram (village, Penlogan cottage at end of village, in St. Ivel parish); St. Ivel (mine); Hillside Farm / Polskiddy Downs; Hamblyn Manor; Treliskey Plantation (gate, stile, Dingley Bottom); Veryan (Methodist chapel); Pentudy; St. Hilary (Bodmin Assizes/gaol); Perranpool; Rostrevor Castle; Boulogne; London (Temple, St. James's Park, Hyde Park, Rotten Row).

## BOOK

**Ch I–II (Gate; Sir John's plans).** Dorothy orders Ralph to open gate; he refuses ("I am not your servant"), jumps stile. She tries Jess at gate; Jess falls, Dorothy unconscious, head bleeding. Ralph's churlishness; he feels guilt. Sir John's motives: debt, marriage to Probus for money, promised directorship; Dorothy's vanity over Probus gifts; Sir John fears "some Romeo". Probus visits; boy reports Dorothy "got killed" near Treliskey.

**Ch III–IV (Carry).** Ralph carries Dorothy ~2 miles; stream revival; she says "Are you taking me home?" Dr. Barrow's carriage; she taken to Hamblyn Manor. Ralph ashamed. Sir John refuses sleep. Ralph confesses to Sir John; Sir John threatens to hold him responsible, calls working class "Board-school" cads, mentions ground rent; Ralph retorts about Sir John cheating David. Ralph walks home through plantation.

**Ch IV–V (Hillside backstory; lives).** David built Hillside 12 years ago, leased on three lives (Julian Seccombe, Doubleday's boy, Billy Penlogan). Billy died (scarlet fever), Doubleday's boy drowned. Lease: "Three lives or nothing." Quarry royalties withheld; Sir John charged for stone. David hid a tin lode (found 7 yrs earlier); told Ralph. Julian wounded, dies; Ralph and David discuss "sufficient unto the day" (Matthew).

**Ch VI–VII (Harvest; Sir John's visit).** Harvest; neighbours' "cutting neck" shout. Sir John comes; David says Julian's death costs them the farm. Sir John lets Hillside to William Jenkins, leaves David rent-free till Michaelmas. Ralph calls it theft of common land (Polskiddy Downs was common). Ralph snaps Sir John's riding-crop across knee. Sir John: "I'll make you suffer." David's pride: "it will break my heart."

**Ch VIII–IX (Departure; Dorothy again).** Agent's repair list torn, distrained. Michaelmas: David has £30 cash left; sells stock at Summercourt Fair. Ralph shows David's tin lode (tree-to-parlour-chimney line, gatepost in Stone Close). Ralph meets Dorothy at Hamblyn lodge gates; she thanks him, takes his hand; she's in bath-chair (white donkey, James). Lord Probus arrives; Ralph leaves. Penlogans move to tiny cottage in St. Goram (St. Ivel parish). Last night at Hillside: David reads Psalm 121, kisses Ruth.

**Ch X (Death; Ralph's threat).** Night: David stroke; writes "I shall die at home. Praise the Lord!"; dies three hours later from second stroke. Ralph storms Manor: "You killed him"; "some day we shall be quits." Gale; branch strikes Ralph in plantation; unconscious; blood on head.

**Ch XI (Dorothy finds Ralph).** Sir John reflects on guilt; fears Ralph's temper. Dorothy tells father her conscience; "I want to do my part in the world"; "I am a woman now." Dorothy finds Ralph with Billy; sends Billy for Dr. Barrow. Ralph delirious: hates the Hamblyns except squire's little maid; "I wish I were rich... we would fight the world together." Dorothy feels new sensation. Dr. Barrow arrives.

**Ch XII (Refusal; Probus).** Dorothy refuses Probus; Probus in London; Sir John fears romance. Dorothy visits Penlogans; Ralph's confession in delirium worries Sir John. Sir John hides from Dorothy that he is the ground landlord. Probus returns; Dorothy confirms "I do not love him"; Probus asks her wait till new year.

**Ch XIII (Shooting).** Sir John shot in Treliskey (left arm, cheek) from hedge; blames Ralph; runs home shouting "Murder." Dr. Barrow: "main volume just missed him." Dorothy visits cottage at night; Ralph: "I am as innocent as you are"; she: "I believe you." Ralph's dread; Ralph's family: mother ill, poverty.

**Ch XIV (Arrest; trial).** Ralph's sister and mother; Ralph claims he shot rabbits in Dingley Bottom. Budda arrests him next morning. Remanded; bail refused. Public hostile. Assizes trial set; Ralph's speech insulting bench ("God will punish him", "Shylock"). Committed for trial on charge of shooting with intent to do grievous bodily harm.

**Ch XV (Sir John angry).** Sir John's evidence; magistrates favour him. Dorothy learns (from newspaper) her father is the ground landlord; she is ashamed. Argument: Dorothy "I know he is innocent"; Sir John: "Go to your room."

**Ch XVI (Workhouse).** Mrs. Penlogan's furniture sold for rent; relieving officer: half a crown a week; Ruth refused sewing job. Mary Penlogan enters workhouse (the "big house"); "I'm just going to be still and wait."

**Ch XVII (Gossip).** William Menire worried for Ruth; goes with Budda to Amos Bice; told cottage emptied, mother in workhouse, Ruth going to service. St. Goram gossip.

**Ch XVIII (Confession).** Vicar John Seccombe reflects. Jim Brewer confesses he shot the squire while poaching (fed family, little Fred ill, Jack, Mary, Peggy). Bilkins admits seeing Jim near plantation with gun (in furze bush). Sir John: "Let the law take its course" then refuses to proceed further: "I'll wash my hands of the whole affair."

**Ch XIX (Release).** Grand Jury throws out bill; Ralph released from Bodmin; William meets him with a rug and breakfast at King's Arms; Ralph weeps. Crowd of St. Goram silent; mother's workhouse fate revealed.

**Ch XX (Ruth in service).** Ruth at William's; mother in workhouse; Ruth in service with the Varcoes (Quakers). William drives Ruth; he's smitten. Ralph: "Honesty sent to prison, and thrift to the workhouse."

**Ch XXI (Mary dies).** Ralph visits Mary; her "good name" speech about David ("He walked with God"). Mary dies; telegram "Your mother found dead in bed." William offers to be banker; funeral; Sir John sends steward.

**Ch XXII (Fresh start).** Ralph works St. Ivel Mine (14s/week, lodges at 8s). Hay job at Hillside for Jenkins (Jenkins uneasy). Peter Ladock hire. Ralph's cottage; Ruth returns Oct 1 with William's trap. Ralph says he'll never marry. Ruth suspects his love for Dorothy.

**Ch XXIII (Concrete).** Ralph's experiments; Perranpool history (fishing village → resort; Brick, Tile, and Clay Company). Ralph makes concrete from waste heap; contractor Robert Telfer finances him; company withdraws; Telfer warns.

**Ch XXIV (Company refuses).** Company (chairman letter) withdraws concession; threatens action. Mary Telfer visits Ruth; Ruth hopes Mary might suit Ralph. Ralph tries to replace Dorothy with Mary in thought. Ralph decides to go to London for counsel (Sir John Liskeard).

**Ch XXV (London).** Liskeard, MP, shows Ralph House of Commons. Ralph follows Dorothy and a slim, bored young man in St. James's Park; she sees him, leaves. Ralph's counsel: strong case, but costs ruinous. Liskeard notes Lord Probus and Lord St. Goram hold shares in the company.

**Ch XXVI (Confession).** Ralph's train home delayed; second Park meeting; Dorothy: "I thought I could not be mistaken!" Ralph tells her he hates her father and loves her; she leaves. Liskeard letter: come again.

**Ch XXVII (Hillside for sale).** Liskeard: Hamblyn selling Hillside freehold through Messrs. Begum & Swear, Chancery Lane. Ralph home; Ruth; visitors at door.

**Ch XXVIII (Sam Tremail).** Sam Tremail (Pentudy, 26, rich, handsome) saw Ruth at the auction; asks William to introduce.

**Ch XXIX (Motives).** William's shop lease refused by Lord St. Goram (punished for County Council vote). Ralph wants Hillside for tin lode. William's temptation; list of propositions; William rejects dishonourable buy. Jenkins wants out.

**Ch XXX (Partnership plan).** William and Ralph discuss Hillside tin lode; William's cautions. Ruth cool with William.

**Ch XXXI (Partnership).** William offers money; Ruth not to know; partnership (handshake). They set to buy Hillside via St. Hilary lawyer.

**Ch XXXII (Missed).** Sir John's letter to Jenkins: Hillside sold. Ralph: "We've missed it." Ralph plans to emigrate; Ruth hurt. Ruth learns William backing.

**Ch XXXIII (Proposal).** Sam proposes to Ruth at cottage; Ruth: "Yes, I will think it over." Sam overhears Ruth; Ruth tells Ralph she has refused Sam (in Ch XXXV). Sam goes to William's shop, boasts.

**Ch XXXIV (Fresh page).** Lawyer Jewell's letter: offer accepted. William rushes to St. Ivel. Ralph relaunches; Jim Brewer hired; Brewer's family food.

**Ch XXXV (Sinking pit).** Jenkins scorns mining; Brewer and Ralph dig; rich samples; Ralph fears assay too rich. Ruth declines Sam. William and Ruth distant.

**Ch XXXVI (Penalty).** Great St. Goram Mine: out-of-works, reporters; Lord St. Goram claims right of way; Chancellor of Duchy; Jenkins compensation. William suggests company. Ralph goes to London; Liskeard to float company; Ralph insists local preference.

**Ch XXXVII (Strength).** Mine in full working by May; Ralph managing director; William secretary; Lord St. Goram shut out of shares. Ralph's moral warning ("workhouse" reminder). William's mother dead; William moves to Veryan. Ruth's unease; William ill (pneumonia).

**Ch XXXVIII (Love).** Ruth realises love for William; William confesses love; "You must not die." He recovers; Ruth promised to William. Ralph sees Dorothy on the stile; Hamblyn Manor empty, Sir John in Boulogne.

**Ch XXXIX (Dorothy).** Dorothy meets Ralph in plantation; recognises him. Dorothy is companion to Dowager Duchess of Flint; Dowager rents Hamblyn Manor. Ralph's thoughts on true aristocracy. Dorothy reflects on Archie Temple.

**Ch XL (Love or farewell).** Ralph goes to church hoping to see Dorothy; Ruth reports Dorothy at Manor. Ralph and Dorothy meet on road; he declares love; she: "Oh, Ralph, let me love you for one brief minute; then we must say farewell for ever!"

**Ch XLI (Tables turned).** Ralph visits Sir John at Boulogne boarding house; refuses permission; hints at rich lode; Sir John begs; Ralph leaves; Sir John misses boat.

**Ch XLII (Coals of fire).** Ralph and Dorothy meet at lodge gates; Dorothy says "Surely we may be friends"; she says father would not allow. Sir John visits Ralph at Penlogan cottage (Hillside? in Ruth's parlour); Ralph forgives, reveals lode, no conditions. Sir John weeps. Dorothy hides, overhears laughter.

**Ch XLIII (Sir John atones).** Sir John remains at Manor; Ralph's deal freed him from money-lenders. Sir John approves Ralph ("shouldn't object to him for a son-in-law"). Dorothy and Ralph meet in plantation; "I have waited long for this day." Dowager needs a new secretary.

---
End of notes.
